s1.syndrome_frame: subacute pulmonary syndrome with weight loss and persistent dry cough
salient_findings: dry cough for 4 weeks
mild weight loss
coarse crepitations over the right upper and lower lung zones
air-space opacity in the right upper lobe on chest radiograph
multifocal consolidations in the right upper lobe extending to the right lower lobe on CT
key_facts: 56-year-old woman
no significant medical history
denies fever, haemoptysis, night sweats
no known contacts with tuberculosis
two courses of antibiotics produced no improvement
Mantoux tuberculin skin test showed 10 mm of induration
sputum induction for acid-fast bacilli was negative
bronchoalveolar lavage was negative for Xpert Mycobacterium tuberculosis/rifampicin assay
bacterial and fungal cultures from bronchoalveolar lavage were negative

shortlist.label: sarcoidosis
shortlist.why_kept: persistent dry cough and weight loss with negative infectious workup

shortlist.label: lymphangitic carcinomatosis
shortlist.why_kept: persistent dry cough and weight loss with multifocal consolidations on CT

shortlist.label: bronchoalveolar cell carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: persistent dry cough and weight loss with negative infectious workup and abnormal CT findings

shortlist.label: organizing pneumonia
shortlist.why_kept: persistent dry cough and weight loss with multifocal consolidations on CT and negative infectious workup

shortlist.label: Wegener's granulomatosis
shortlist.why_kept: persistent dry cough and weight loss with negative infectious workup and abnormal CT findings

raw.rationale: The patient's symptoms of dry cough and mild weight loss, lack of response to antibiotics, and radiographic findings of multifocal consolidations are consistent with organizing pneumonia. The negative tests for tuberculosis and other infections also support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: sarcoidosis
rejected.why: While possible, the lack of other systemic symptoms and the specific radiographic pattern make it less likely

rejected.label: lymphangitic carcinomatosis
rejected.why: There is no mention of a known primary malignancy, making this diagnosis less likely

rejected.label: bronchoalveolar cell carcinoma
rejected.why: The radiographic findings and clinical presentation do not strongly suggest a malignant process

rejected.label: Wegener's granulomatosis
rejected.why: The absence of systemic symptoms such as fever, haemoptysis, and night sweats, and the lack of renal involvement make this diagnosis less likely
